title: Mechanical tracing of protein function in the Drosophila ear
protocol: Calibrate the Brüel & Kjaer pressure microphone using the acoustic calibrator.
Generate a 1 kHz tone of 94 dB SPL with the calibrator.
Sample the output voltage signal of the microphone.
Cut the time trace into _N_ time windows, each of length _T = 1 s_.
Set the sampling frequency to 4096 or 8192 Hz.
Choose the number of samples per window to be a power of two (2^12 or 2^13).
Apply Fast Fourier transformation analysis to determine the Fourier amplitude at 1 kHz.
Place the pressure microphone and the reference microphone side by side in the acoustic far field of a loudspeaker.
Generate a continuous 1 kHz signal with the function generator.
Pass the generated signal through the step attenuator.
Pass the signal from the step attenuator through the audio amplifier.
Broadcast the signal via the loudspeaker.
Sample the output signals of both microphones.
Subject the sampled signals to Fast Fourier transforms.
Determine the respective Fourier amplitudes at 1 kHz.
Heat the soldering iron to approximately 220°C.
Briefly anesthetize the fly with CO₂.
Melt a drop of wax at the tip of the Teflon rod.
Use tweezers to hold the fly by its wings and attach it to the rod using the melted wax, ensuring its legs are free.
Wax the fly's coxae to the rod carefully with fine tips of the soldering iron to fix the thorax, orienting the arista perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the rod.
Avoid touching the antenna with the wire to prevent damage to the ear.
Attach small drops of wax to the postero-lateral side of the head and stabilize the halteres, wing-hinges, and proboscis.
Blow on the antenna to test its movement and ensure it has not been damaged during preparation.
Arrange the setup on the vibration isolation table with the laser Doppler vibrometer positioned in the center.
Mount the rod holding the fly on a micromanipulator.
Position the manipulator so that the fly is at the focal distance from the LDV.
Turn the rod to orient the arista of one antenna perpendicular to the optical axis of the laser.
Focus the laser on the tip of the arista using the coaxial video capture system.
Adjust the position via the scanning unit until a maximum level of backscattered laser light is obtained.
Place the loudspeaker at a distance of approximately 10 cm behind the fly, facing both the LDV and the fly.
Use a second micromanipulator to bring the reference microphone close to the measured antenna (distance about 5 mm).
Ensure that the measured arista and the microphone are equidistant from the loudspeaker.
Make sure the microphone membrane is perpendicular to the direction of sound propagation.
